claim: Did you know… strangers' distant healing helped patients with advanced AIDS?

studies.cite: Sicher et al. (1998), Western Journal of Medicine
studies.finding: In 40 patients with advanced AIDS, ten weeks of distant healing was followed by fewer new illnesses and hospital days.
studies.verdict: Small trial; a later larger one found nothing.

studies.cite: Astin et al. (2006), Alternative Therapies in Health and Medicine
studies.finding: A randomized trial of 156 HIV/AIDS patients found no effect of distant healing on any primary or secondary outcome.

claim: Did you know… you can feel when someone is staring at you?

studies.cite: Schmidt et al. (2004), British Journal of Psychology
studies.finding: A meta-analysis of 15 remote-staring experiments found a small mean effect on skin conductance, d = 0.13.
studies.verdict: Authors saw hints of an effect but few independent replications.

studies.cite: Colwell, Schröder & Sladen (2000), British Journal of Psychology
studies.finding: Accuracy beat chance only with feedback on non-random trial sequences; with truly random sequences, accuracy fell to chance.
studies.verdict: Pattern learning, not a staring sense.

claim: Did you know… dying patients float out of their bodies and see hidden images?

studies.finding: Across 2,060 cardiac arrests, 2% of 101 interviewed survivors described awareness of the resuscitation, and images were placed on high shelves to test it.
studies.verdict: No patient reported the hidden images; test inconclusive.

claim: Did you know… practitioners can feel a human energy field with their hands?

studies.finding: Twenty-one Therapeutic Touch practitioners tried to tell which of their hands the tester hovered over, behind a screen.
studies.verdict: Correct in 44% of 280 trials, below chance.
